criteria.criterion: `judge` in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs counts a cited command as seen when it equals a command the verifier ran, or equals one whole simple command inside a compound the verifier ran (split on `&&`, `;`, `||`, `|`), after trimming and collapsing whitespace. Split on shell separators as policy.rs does, and never match inside quotes. A trailing output filter such as `| tail -n 30` on a ran command does not hide the cited command before it.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The new `simple_commands` in verify.rs splits on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` and newlines; these are the separators policy.rs lists on line 6. It tracks single and double quotes so it never splits inside them, collapses whitespace outside quotes, and strips a trailing ` 2>&1`. `judge` now builds its ran list with flat_map(simple_commands). A citation counts as seen when all of its simple commands are in that list, so `X 2>&1 | tail -n 30` yields `X`.

criteria.criterion: Matching stays strict where it matters: a cited command with different arguments, a different test filter, or a different package is still unseen. A command the verifier never ran is still reported as 'cited but not seen running' and the criterion is still unmet.
criteria.evidence: Matching is still exact equality on the pieces, with no prefix or substring match. The test `cited_commands_with_other_arguments_or_never_run_stay_unseen` asserts that a different filter (`other`), a different package (`athena-agent`), a never-run command (`cargo clippy`), a prefix (`cargo test --locked`), text inside quotes and an empty citation all fail. The finding text for unrun commands and the unmet logic are unchanged; the existing test `a_criterion_citing_a_command_that_never_ran_is_unmet` and the lifecycle test still pass.

findings.summary: The splitter is a second, simpler tokenizer next to the one in policy.rs, so the two can drift apart.
findings.evidence: policy.rs has its own segment tokenizer (around lines 190-310), which handles comments, `|&` and redirections. verify.rs adds a separate splitter. They agree on the main separators, but a later change to one would not reach the other.

findings.summary: A piece can match even when its context changes its meaning, for example `cd other && cargo test`.
findings.evidence: If the verifier ran `cd sub && cargo test`, a citation of `cargo test` counts as seen, although it ran in a different directory. The policy's directory confinement limits the harm.

findings.summary: A compound citation counts as seen if its pieces ran separately.
findings.evidence: A citation is seen when all of its pieces are in the flattened ran list. So `cargo test | grep ok` counts as seen if `cargo test` and `grep ok` ran as separate commands. This is still evidence of running, but the pipeline itself never ran.

summary: I find that the change fixes the cause in the reading. Before it, `judge` in verify.rs matched a cited command only against the whole command line the verifier ran, so a command run in a chain or piped to `tail` counted as unseen. Now both the cited command and each ran command are split into simple commands on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` and newlines. Quoted text is never split, whitespace is collapsed and a trailing `2>&1` is dropped. A citation counts as seen only if every one of its pieces equals a piece that ran. Strictness holds: my test runs show that a different filter, a different package, a prefix, text inside quotes, an empty citation and a never-run command all stay unseen. The new tests would fail under the old exact match; the `&&` and `| tail` cases show it. A new decision, D63, amends D43. The design doc, the verifier prompt and the CHANGELOG (under Unreleased / Changed) are updated to match. I ran `cargo test --locked -p athena-core verify` (5 tests pass), `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`; all passed. Three findings are minor and none blocks: the splitter duplicates the tokenizer in policy.rs, and two loosenings are possible (described in the findings). policy.rs and lifecycle.rs were listed as deliverables but left unchanged. That fits the out-of-scope note, which says not to change the policy unless tests show a gap.
